keyPhrases.text: Most of the time this kind of experiment doesn't work
the background element of family wrath tends to shrivel
Some of the performances are uneven
moments in the production, particularly in the first act, feel flat
the production moves solidly through the binding force of director Peter Hall's theatrical intelligence
the sweeping, intricate pace never sags
there are specifics, those fresh moments an audience hopes for
Any number of affecting touches from Lynn Colleens' Juliet
No small tribute is owed Gunter's fluid, elegant set
the black portion of the cast is magisterial
reminds us of why 'Romeo & Juliet' remains a classic

reasoning: Mixed review with significant praise for direction, pacing, specific performances, and technical elements, balanced against notable criticisms of the casting concept, uneven performances, and problematic lead actor. No explicit recommendation but appreciative of the production's strengths while acknowledging substantial flaws.
